text:
President Donald Trump made a jab at his own cabinet by joking about falling asleep during their last meeting, which he called "pretty boring."

"Last time we had a press conference it lasted for 3 hours. And some people said, 'He closed his eyes!' Look, it got pretty boring, in all fairness," the president said.

"I love these people... there's a lot of people, it was a little bit of the boring side, but I didn't fall sleep, I just closed them because I wanted to get the hell out of here," Trump said.

The cabinet meets often last hours. The Aug. 26 Cabinet meeting lasted for 3 hours and 17 minutes, the longest so far. Trump's Dec. 2 meeting lasted two hours and 18 minutes with the president visibly struggling to keep his eyes open throughout the remarks from his Cabinet members.

“It’s boring as hell," Trump told New York Magazine in an interview published earlier this week. "I’m going around a room, and I’ve got 28 guys — the last one was three and a half hours. I have to sit back and listen, and I move my hand so that people will know I’m listening. I’m hearing every word, and I can’t wait to get out."

The Trump administration held its 10th publicly known Cabinet meeting amid simmering tensions over the federal immigration crackdown in Minneapolis, Minnesota, where federal immigration agents shot down two U.S. citizens this month.

Homeland Security Secretary Kristi Noem is facing calls to resign. On Tuesday, Sens. Thom Tillis and Lisa Murkowski called for Noem to step down.

Tillis, R-N.C., told reporters on Capitol Hill that he did not have confidence in Noem and that "she should go."

Minnesota's chief federal judge excoriated ICE on Wednesday, saying the agency had violated nearly 100 court orders and had defied more judicial directives in January alone than “some federal agencies have violated in their entire existence.”

Trump's "border czar," Tom Homan, who was deployed to Minneapolis after Gregory Bovino, the U.S. Border Patrol chief, left the city along with some of his agents after the killing of 37-year-old Alex Pretti, a VA nurse and U.S. citizen.

Addressing his first news conference in Minneapolis on Thursday Homan said he would be "staying till the problem's gone," adding that he has ordered federal immigration authorities to work on a “drawdown plan” for law enforcement in Minnesota.

Homan said neither he nor President Trump wants anyone to die, but stressed that “the hostile rhetoric and dangerous threats and hate” against immigration enforcement agents “must stop.”
